source_text: IV. Quodam autem tempore media nocte, residente pro tribunali praeside Probo, introductus est iterum beatissimus martyr Irenaeus. Probus dixit ad eum: Iam sacrifica, Irenaee, lucrans poenas. Irenaeus respondit: Fac quod iussum est, hoc a me non exspectes. Probus indignatus eum fustibus caedi praecepit. Irenaeus respondit: Deum habeo, quem a prima aetate colere didici: ipsum adoro, qui me confortat in omnibus, cui etiam et sacrifico; deos vero manu factos adorare non possum. Probus dixit: Lucrare mortem. iam tibi sufficiant quae tolerasti tormenta. Irenaeus respondit: Lucror continuo mortem quando per eas quas mihi putas inferre poenas, quas ego non sentio, propter deum accipio vitam aeternam. Probus dixit: Uxorem habes? Irenaeus respondit: Non habeo. Probus dixit: Filios habes? Irenaeus respondit: Non habeo. Probus dixit: Parentes habes? Irenaeus respondit: Non habeo. Probus dixit: Et qui fuerunt illi qui praeterita flebant sessione? Irenaeus respondit: Praeceptum est domini mei Iesu Christi dicentis: Qui diligit patrem aut matrem aut uxorem aut filios aut fratres aut parentes super me, non est me dignus. itaque ad deum in caelum adspiciens et ad eius promissiones intendens, omnia despiciens nullum parentem absque eo se nosse atque habere fatebatur. Probus dixit: Vel propter illos sacrifica. Irenaeus respondit: Filii mei deum habent quem et ego, qui potest illos salvare. tu autem fac quod tibi praeceptum est. Probus dixit: Consule tibi, iuvenis. immola, ut non te cruciatibus impendam. Irenaeus respondit: Fac quod vis. iam nunc videbis quantam mihi dominus Iesus Christus dabit tolerantiam adversus tuas insidias. Probus dixit: Dabo in te sententiam. Irenaeus respondit: Gratulor si feceris. Probus data sententia dixit: Irenaeum inobedientem praeceptis regalibus in fluvium praecipitari iubeo. Irenaeus respondit: Multifarias minas tuas et tormenta plurima exspectabam, ut etiam post haec me ferro subiiceres. tu autem nihil horum intulisti. unde hoc facias oro, ut cognoscas quemadmodum Christiani propter fidem, quae est in deo, mortem contemnere consueverunt.
thought_title: Night hearing, refusal of family ties, and sentence to drowning
orientation: Governor Probus questions Irenaeus again at midnight after prison torture and presses him to offer sacrifice.
pass_a_gloss: Now at a certain time in the middle of the night, with Governor Probus sitting before the tribunal, the most blessed martyr Irenaeus was led in again. Probus said to him: Now offer sacrifice, Irenaeus, gaining punishments. Irenaeus answered: Do what has been ordered, do not expect this from me. Probus in anger ordered him to be beaten with clubs. Irenaeus answered: I have God, whom I learned to worship from my earliest age: him I adore, who strengthens me in all things, to whom also I offer sacrifice; but gods made by hand I cannot adore. Probus said: Gain death. Let the torture which you have endured now be enough for you. Irenaeus answered: I gain death continually when through those punishments which you think to bring upon me, which I do not feel, on account of God I receive eternal life. Probus said: Do you have a wife? Irenaeus answered: I do not have. Probus said: Do you have children? Irenaeus answered: I do not have. Probus said: Do you have parents? Irenaeus answered: I do not have. Probus said: And who were those who wept at the previous hearing? Irenaeus answered: It is the command of my lord Jesus Christ saying: Who loves father or mother or wife or children or brothers or parents above me, is not worthy of me. And so looking to God into heaven and directing attention to his promises, despising all things, he confessed that he knew and had no parent apart from him. Probus said: At least on account of them offer sacrifice. Irenaeus answered: My children have God whom I also have, who is able to save them. But you do what has been commanded to you. Probus said: Take counsel for yourself, young man. Offer sacrifice, lest I hang you in tortures. Irenaeus answered: Do what you wish. Even now you will see how great endurance the Lord Jesus Christ will give me against your plots. Probus said: I will give sentence against you. Irenaeus answered: I rejoice if you shall do it. Probus when sentence was given said: I order Irenaeus disobedient to the royal commands to be thrown into the river. Irenaeus answered: I was expecting your threats of many kinds and very many torture, that also after these you would subject me to the sword. But you have brought in none of these. Therefore I beg that you do this, that you may learn in what manner Christians on account of the faith which is in God are accustomed to despise death.

choices.why: brief glossary fixes sacrificare to offer sacrifice
keeps dii as gods and avoids hyphenated compound
brief glossary fixes tormenta to torture
brief glossary fixes tolerantia to endurance
brief glossary fixes vitam aeternam to eternal life

pass_b_english: One night, at midnight, Governor Probus took his seat at the tribunal, and the most blessed martyr Irenaeus was brought in again. Probus said to him, "Now offer sacrifice, Irenaeus, and escape punishment." Irenaeus answered, "Do what you have been ordered to do. Do not expect this from me." In anger Probus ordered him to be beaten with clubs. Irenaeus answered, "I have God, whom I have learned to worship since my earliest childhood. I worship him, for he strengthens me in everything, and to him I also offer sacrifice. But I cannot worship gods made by hand."

Probus said, "You are earning death for yourself. Let the torture you have already endured be enough for you." Irenaeus answered, "I gain death again and again, for through these punishments you think you bring upon me, which I do not feel, I receive eternal life for God's sake." Probus said, "Do you have a wife?" Irenaeus answered, "I do not." Probus said, "Do you have children?" Irenaeus answered, "I do not." Probus said, "Do you have parents?" Irenaeus answered, "I do not." Probus said, "Then who were those who wept at the last hearing?" Irenaeus answered, "My Lord Jesus Christ gave this command, saying, 'Whoever loves father or mother or wife or children or brothers or parents more than me is not worthy of me' (Matthew 10:37)." He looked up to God in heaven and fixed his mind on his promises. Despising all else, he declared that he knew and had no parent apart from him.

Probus said, "At least for their sake offer sacrifice." Irenaeus answered, "My children have God, whom I also have, and he can save them. But you, do what has been commanded to you." Probus said, "Take thought for yourself, young man. Offer sacrifice, so I will not hand you over to torture." Irenaeus answered, "Do what you wish. You will see right now what great endurance the Lord Jesus Christ will give me against your plots." Probus said, "I will pass sentence upon you." Irenaeus answered, "I shall be glad if you do." After giving sentence Probus said, "I order Irenaeus, disobedient to the imperial commands, to be thrown into the river." Irenaeus answered, "I expected many threats from you and much torture, and that after this you would also put me to the sword. You have brought none of these upon me. So I beg you to do this, that you may learn how Christians, through faith which is in God, are accustomed to despise death."
